decisions.summary: the berm was built for every supply canal (head race, canals A and B), not canal A alone
decisions.why: 0055 says every supply canal; building for canal A alone would have been the carve-out. Its own cost was measured (canal A only 48 -> 42) and not taken.

decisions.id: W74-b revert and re-tier E2 -> E3
decisions.summary: the built berm (bank median 5.04 / 5.02 ft) is reverted because the 48-seed cohort went 48 -> 46; the row stays open (kept) at E3, its work the layouts that broke
decisions.why: The spec's Assumptions say a wave that finds a row harder than ranked moves it down and says so. The Edge Case 'a fix that changes many maps' says the row takes that work's tier and its claim stays as found. The newly refused seeds fail in web, row_rules and water_rules, outside pockets.py, which is a change across modules: E3 by FR-003. Ranking by measured work is the request's own principle, and reverting keeps a measured regression off main (XIII). The row is not deferred or dropped, so the request's 'fix all of it' still reaches it in E3 order. Record note: the Edge Case's 'waits on a found row' is met by the row's own fix text rather than an 'after' entry, the same as wave 69's row.

decisions.id: W74-c failed fix recorded and patch kept
decisions.summary: _outside_command's docstring records the failed fix; the patch and its tests are kept in audit/reverted/
decisions.why: Constitution XIV (a fix that failed is recorded at the point of change). The patch holds partition.py, pockets.py and the two test files the docstring names.

decisions.id: W74-d _water's drift left to its row

decisions.why: It was already a ranked row in tier order, not a finding the wave introduced.
